# What drives the increase in girth?

<!-- STEP id="return-to-the" -->
Return to the stem cross-section. The dividing cells form a continuous cylinder rather than a pocket at the tip.

<!-- STEP id="this-side-running" -->
This side-running cylinder of dividing cells that increases stem and root diameter is called the **lateral meristem**.

<!-- STEP id="like-adding-fresh" -->
Like adding fresh layers beneath the surface of a wooden pencil, new material increases the outside diameter instead of merely stretching what already exists. The comparison ends there because a pencil is assembled once, whereas living stems keep producing new cells over many years.
